title: Access computation returns the indexed bit
statement: Let $z$ be a finite bit string, $r$ a natural number, and $\mathrm{mode}$ a Boolean. For every natural number $k$ with $k\le |z|$ and $k\le r$, there are natural numbers $k'$ and $p'$ such that, from the configuration on input $\langle z,\mathrm{bits}(r)\rangle$ with the access machine in its initial scan state, there is a finite safe computation to a halting configuration that outputs the bit $\mathrm{mode}\land(r<|z|)$ if $\mathrm{mode}$ is true, and otherwise outputs the $r$-th bit of $z$, using false when that position is beyond the end of $z$.
